title: Cyber — Network Security Coverage, Endorsement 7 (Policy B)

clauses.heading: Insuring Agreement A
clauses.text: We will pay Loss resulting from a Network Security Event first discovered during the Policy Period.

clauses.heading: Exclusion 4(f)
clauses.text: This Policy does not apply to Loss arising out of the Insured's failure to maintain the Minimum Security Standards.

clauses.heading: Endorsement 7
clauses.text: Exclusion 4(f) shall not apply to Loss resulting from a Network Security Event occurring while the Insured maintained the Minimum Security Standards.

clauses.heading: Definitions — Minimum Security Standards
clauses.text: "Minimum Security Standards" means the controls listed in Schedule B, maintained continuously.

plain_english_why: Exclusion 4(f) applies only to claims where the Insured FAILED to maintain the Minimum Security Standards. Endorsement 7 restores coverage only for claims where the Insured MAINTAINED them — and the definition of Minimum Security Standards ("maintained continuously") makes maintaining and failing to maintain mutually exclusive. So every claim Endorsement 7 would give back was never excluded in the first place. The set of claims it restores is empty: the carveback is illusory. The policy reads as if Endorsement 7 broadens coverage; it broadens nothing.
